newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's investors paid too much in auctions -agent.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's investors paid too much in auctions -agent.

text.p: Some participants in last year's Lloyds of London's auctions paid too much for 1997 capacity in the insurance market, members' agency LRG Cater Allen said on Friday.

"Some buyers paid thousands of pounds more than was necessary to obtain capacity on syndicates in the 1996 auctions," the agency said in a statement accompanying the publication of its Market & Auction Review.
Last year saw the second round of Lloyd's auctions in which investors in the market can buy and sell participations in insurance syndicates for the next year.
LRG's review, called 'The Guide', also said that some managing agents, which manage syndicates, "created respectable average auction prices by buying their own capacity at unnecessary prices."
David Gittings, Lloyd's director of regulatory services, said last month that stricter surveillance of the auctions would be introduced following concerns about insider dealing.

LRG Cater Allen also noted that corporate investors, who have steadily been replacing traditional individual Names since 1994, acquired two thirds much of their 1.5 billion stg ($2.4 billion) 1997 capacity increase outside the auctions.
Lloyd's has capacity -- the maximum amount of premium income it can underwrite -- of some 10.3 billion stg this year
In addition to commenting on the auctions, the review looks at the flurry of merger and acquisition activity among Lloyd's managing agencies during the last nine months.

"Those that have attracted most attention have been LIMIT's acquisition of interests in Bankside and Janson Green, ACE's acquisition of interests in Methuen and the Ockham managing agents, Archer's link-up with Chartwell Re, CLM's acquisitive actions."

LIMIT is the largest of the original corporate investors which entered the market in 1994, while Bermudan based ACE Limited now controls the largest managing agency grouping in Lloyd's, with around 0.75 billion of market capacity.
LRG Cater Allen, which is part of Cater Allen Holdings Plc, said it planned a more detailed look at these corporate changes in its forthcoming guide to the 1997 underwriting market.
-- Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769 ($ = 0.619 British Pounds Sterling)
